{{short description|French, German, and Israeli researcher in quantum computing}}
[[File:Julia Kempe.jpg|thumb|Julia Kempe]]
'''Julia Kempe''' is a French, German, and Israeli researcher in [[quantum computing]].{{r|feo}} She is currently the Director of the [[New York University Center for Data Science]] and Professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]].{{r|cds}}

==Education and career==
Kempe was born in [[East Berlin]], to a family of Russian descent.{{r|cim}} She moved to Austria in 1990,{{r|pain}} and did her undergraduate studies in mathematics and physics at the [[University of Vienna]] from 1992 to 1995, with a year as an exchange student in physics at the [[University of Technology Sydney]]. She then earned two [[Master of Advanced Studies]] (DEA) degrees in France: one in mathematics in 1996 from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] and another in 1997 in physics from the ''[[École normale supérieure]]''. She completed two doctorates in 2001. The dissertation for her Ph.D. in computer science from the ''[[Télécom ParisTech|École nationale supérieure des télécommunications]]'' was entitled ''Quantum Computing: Random Walks and Entanglement'', and was supervised by Gérard Cohen. Her second Ph.D., in mathematics, was from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], with a dissertation entitled ''Universal Noiseless Quantum Computation: Theory and Applications'' and was jointly supervised by [[Elwyn Berlekamp]] and chemist [[K. Birgitta Whaley]].{{r|cv}}

She joined CNRS at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in 2001
(overlapping with postdoctoral studies at Berkeley and the Berkeley [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]]), joined the [[Tel Aviv University]] faculty in 2007{{r|tau}}, and moved her CNRS position from Paris-Sud to Paris Diderot in 2010.{{r|cv}}.  Between 2011 and 2018 she was a researcher in finance.{{r|cv}} She became director of the Center of Data Science at NYU and a professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]] in September 2018.{{r|cds}}

==Awards and honors==
In 2006, Kempe won the bronze medal of CNRS and the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] of the French government.{{r|cim|pijc}} In 2009 she won the Krill Prize of the [[Wolf Foundation]],{{r|krill}} and in 2010 she won the ''Trophée des femmes en or'' (English: {{ill|"Women in Gold" trophy|fr|Trophée des femmes en or}} ) for her research.{{r|feo}} In 1998 she received a reward from ''[[Studienstiftung|Studienstiftung des Deutschen Volkes]]'' (English: "German Academic Scholarship Foundation") which was awarded to only 0.25% of students at the time.{{Ref|doj|[10]|noid=doj}} She became a knight in the [[National Order of Merit (France)|National Order of Merit]] in 2010.{{r|cv}} In 2018, she was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].{{r|ae}}
